Visit note | 2025-03-01 11:00 AM | Dr. Farhana Kabir, General Medicine | Patient: Parvin Bepari, 41, female. Mrs. Bepari returns for review, stating she still suffers from brittle nails and constant tiredness. Her symptoms worsened after a long spell of poor meals while living alone in Farmgate. She works as a delivery rider and has no known comorbidity. She denies chest pain, dizziness, or shortness of breath at rest. On examination: haemoglobin 9.1 g/dL, BP 113/72 mmHg, pulse 81 bpm, weight 58 kg. Her mucous membranes appear pale. Assessment: Iron deficiency anaemia. Plan: a prescription was issued for ongoing management. She was advised to eat more lentils, spinach, liver, and eggs, and to avoid tea within an hour of meals. Follow-up in 6 weeks with a repeat haemoglobin test.

Visit note | 2025-03-01 11:30 AM | Dr. Nusrat Jahan, General Medicine | Patient: Hasina Khan, 45, female. Ms. Khan presents with brittle nails, getting breathless on the stairs, and constant tiredness. She mentions that her condition worsened after a long spell of poor meals while living alone in Uttara. She is employed as a police constable and has no history of chronic medical illness. She reports no palpitations, fever, or joint pain. On examination: haemoglobin 8.3 g/dL, BP 132/72 mmHg, pulse 90 bpm, weight 67 kg. Pallor is noted on the conjunctiva. Assessment: Iron deficiency anaemia. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to eat more lentils, spinach, liver, and eggs, and avoid drinking tea within an hour of meals. Follow-up in 6 weeks with a repeat haemoglobin.

Visit note | 2025-03-01 11:30 AM | Dr. Zahid Hasan, Gastroenterology | Patient: Rupa Ahmed, 63, female. Mrs. Ahmed describes pain that eases after eating, gnawing pain in the upper belly, and pain that wakes them at night. She notes that the discomfort started after weeks of taking painkillers for back pain in Bogura. She works as a homemaker and has no other major illnesses. She denies vomiting blood, black stools, or unintended weight loss. On examination: pain score 7/10, BP 131/85 mmHg, pulse 70 bpm, weight 56 kg. Abdominal examination reveals mild epigastric tenderness with no guarding. Assessment: Peptic ulcer disease. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid painkillers such as ibuprofen, stop smoking, and eat regular meals. Follow-up in 4 weeks with a stool H. pylori test.
